content: CD18 integrin beta-2 is a protein in humans encoded by the ITGB2 gene. This protein serves as the beta subunit in four distinct integrin structures: LFA-1 (paired with CD11a), Macrophage-1 antigen (paired with CD11b), integrin alphaXbeta2 (paired with CD11c), and integrin alphaDbeta2 (paired with CD11d). The ITGB2 protein product is the integrin beta chain beta-2. Integrins are integral cell-surface proteins composed of an alpha chain and a beta chain. A single chain can pair with multiple partners, resulting in the formation of different integrins. For instance, the beta-2 chain pairs with the alpha-L chain to form the integrin LFA-1 and pairs with the alpha-M chain to form the integrin Mac-1. Integrins play critical roles in cell adhesion and cell-surface-mediated signaling. In humans, a deficiency of CD18 leads to Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency (LAD), a condition characterized by the inability of leukocytes to extravasate from the bloodstream into tissues. Additionally, beta-2 integrins have been identified in a soluble form. These soluble beta-2 integrins retain ligand-binding capabilities, and their plasma levels are inversely correlated with disease activity in the autoimmune condition spondyloarthritis. CD18 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including FHL2, GNB2L1, ICAM-1, and PSCD1.
